content:
Based on my analysis:

**Test image observations:**
- Lower stem close-up at/near soil level
- Irregular dark brown to black blotches on the stem tissue
- Some reddish/orange coloration visible within the dark lesions
- Late-season context (dried pods and plant material surrounding)

**Candidate reasoning:**
- **Anthracnose**: "Irregularly shaped red to dark brown blotches on stems and petioles; near maturity, black fungal bodies" — matches very well
- **Phytophthora**: Shows dark brown lesion extending up from taproot as a more uniform band — the Phytophthora reference shows more of a girdling lesion pattern, less matching
- **Charcoal_Rot**: The reference shows a silver-gray charcoal-like appearance, clearly different from the dark brown/black irregular blotches in the test image

The dark, irregular brown-to-black blotches on the lower stem in a late-season context is characteristic of Anthracnose stem blight.

The reddish-brown to dark brown discoloration pattern matches the Anthracnose reference images closely. Charcoal_Rot was ruled out (wrong color — silvery/gray), and Phytophthora shows a more uniform girdling lesion rather than irregular blotches."}
